title: "data.frame() changes column names without telling you"
ref: DF-04
categories: [Data frames and lists]
impact: incoherent
extrait: 'names(data.frame("2024" = 1))'
reponse: '"X2024"'
attendu: "`\"my column\" \"2024\" \"a\" \"a\"`"
versions: "All"
source: "General R knowledge"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
tab <- data.frame("my column" = 1, "2024" = 2, "a" = 3, "a" = 4)
names(tab)
tab$`my column`
```
:::

## Why

`data.frame()` has a `check.names = TRUE` argument that runs the names through `make.names()` then `make.unique()`. A space becomes a dot, a name starting with a digit gets an `X` in front, and a duplicate gets a `.1` suffix. `read.csv()` and `read.table()` do the same to the file headers.

Code that then looks up the column under its real name gets `NULL`, with no error.

## The remedy

Turn the correction off when you care about the original names, and write them between backticks.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
tab <- data.frame("my column" = 1, "2024" = 2, check.names = FALSE)
names(tab)
tab$`my column`
```
:::
